ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Sick Visit — Sugar Ray Robinson

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for nausea and dizziness on donepezil

text.paragraph: Nausea, loose stools and dizziness for five days. [S]

Sugar Ray Robinson came in without an appointment with his care partner because of nausea, poor appetite and three or four loose stools a day for five days, with one episode of vomiting yesterday and dizziness when he stands up. Donepezil was raised from 5 mg to 10 mg at bedtime nine days ago; the symptoms began four days later. He has had vivid dreams since the increase. He has kept drinking water but has eaten little, and has kept taking metformin and lisinopril. No fever, blood in the stool, abdominal pain, chest pain or fainting. His home glucose readings have been 100 to 140 mg/dL. Nobody else at home is ill. [S]

list.item:
Donepezil side effects with mild dehydration (R11.0). Cholinergic side effects of the higher donepezil dose: nausea, loose stools, vivid dreams and a slow pulse, with a standing drop in blood pressure and mild dehydration (creatinine 1.2 mg/dL, from 1.0). Sodium, potassium and glucose are safe. ECG shows sinus bradycardia without heart block. No sign of infection. [S]
Donepezil back to 5 mg, taken in the morning with breakfast.
Hold metformin and lisinopril for 48 hours, then restart once he is eating and drinking (sick-day rules).
Small frequent drinks with salt and sugar; bland food.
Check glucose twice daily while metformin is held.
Return or call at once for fainting, a pulse below 50, vomiting that will not stop, or confusion worse than usual.

Alzheimer's disease with early onset (G30.0). Donepezil 5 mg was tolerated for five weeks; a later trial of 10 mg in the morning, or a switch to a rivastigmine patch, can be discussed at the next visit. [S]
Continue donepezil 5 mg each morning.
